questions.q: What is the specific term for the art and science of installing pipes, fixtures, and other apparatus in buildings for bringing in water supply and removing waterborne waste?
questions.n: Plumbing is defined as the comprehensive art and science of installing both water supply and waste removal systems.

questions.q: In the context of water sources, what is another name for 'Free Water'?
questions.n: Free water is also known as gravitational water because it is the water that moves through the soil under the influence of gravity.

questions.q: What device is specifically installed in a piping system to absorb hydraulic shock waves and eliminate 'water hammer'?
questions.n: An arrester is the specialized device designed to cushion the pressure surge when water flow is suddenly stopped.

questions.q: What occurs when the pressure of a nonpotable water system exceeds the positive pressure in the water distribution lines, potentially contaminating the supply?
questions.n: Backpressure happens when the pressure in the downstream system (nonpotable) becomes higher than the upstream supply pressure.

questions.q: Which specific plumbing component serves as a vertical vent pipe primarily to provide air circulation and prevent trap seals from being broken by siphonage?
questions.n: The vent stack is the main vertical pipe installed specifically for air circulation throughout the drainage system.

questions.q: In electrical systems, which unit is defined as the measure of potential difference or electromotive force (EMF)?
questions.n: The volt is the standard unit used to measure the 'pressure' or potential difference in an electric circuit.

questions.q: What electrical condition is characterized specifically by having very low resistance and resulting in a very high current flow?
questions.n: A short circuit creates a path of least resistance, which causes the current to spike to dangerous levels.

questions.q: The term 'Impedance' used in AC circuits (transformers and motors) is a combination of which two factors?
questions.n: Impedance is the total opposition to current in an AC circuit, combining standard resistance and frequency-dependent reactance.

questions.q: What is the name of the automatic air-conditioning system that regulates the quantity of air supplied to each zone based on the local thermal load?
questions.n: A VAV system saves energy by adjusting the amount of air flow to meet the specific cooling or heating needs of a zone.

questions.q: Who is primarily responsible for ensuring the correct dimensions and alignment of an elevator shaft in a building project?
questions.n: The general contractor is in charge of site execution, including the precision of structural shafts for equipment installation.

questions.q: What is the term for the water supply pipe that extends from the water main to the building served?
questions.n: This specific pipe connects the public water main to the individual building's plumbing system.

questions.q: Which type of water is held in the soil against the pull of gravity and is important for plant growth but not usually a source for wells?
questions.n: Capillary water is held in the small pores of the soil by surface tension, resisting gravity.

questions.q: In a drainage system, what is the 'Common Vent' designed to serve?
o: Two fixtures at the same level
questions.n: A common vent (or dual vent) connects at the junction of two fixture drains to serve both simultaneously.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Circuit Vent' in a plumbing installation?
o: To prevent backflow in the main
To vent a single battery of fixtures
To provide a backup air source
questions.n: A circuit vent serves a battery of fixtures and extends from in front of the last fixture connection to the vent stack.

questions.q: Which electrical component is used to change the voltage of an alternating current (AC) circuit?
questions.n: Transformers use electromagnetic induction to step up or step down voltage levels in AC systems.

questions.q: In the context of electrical conductors, how does the length of a wire affect its resistance?
o: Length has no effect on resistance
questions.n: A longer conductor provides more material for electrons to pass through, resulting in higher total resistance.

questions.q: What device provides a constant voltage supply even when the input line voltage varies?
questions.n: A voltage regulator automatically maintains a steady voltage level to protect sensitive equipment.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a 'Soil Pipe' and a 'Waste Pipe'?
o: Soil pipes carry discharge containing fecal matter
Waste pipes carry discharge from water closets
questions.n: The presence of human waste from fixtures like water closets or urinals distinguishes soil pipes from waste pipes.

questions.q: Which elevator component acts as a safety device to stop and hold the elevator car if it exceeds a predetermined speed?
questions.n: The governor triggers the safety brakes (safeties) if the elevator car travels too fast.

questions.q: What is the function of an 'Air Gap' in a plumbing system?
o: To increase water pressure at the fixture
To allow air to enter the vent stack
To muffle the sound of rushing water
To provide a physical separation to prevent backflow
questions.n: An air gap is the most reliable way to prevent cross-connection by ensuring water cannot be siphoned back into the supply.

questions.q: What characterizes an 'Indirect Waste' pipe?
o: It is another name for a vent pipe
It connects directly to the building's drainage system
It does not connect directly to the drainage system
questions.n: Indirect waste pipes discharge into a plumbing fixture or receptacle through an air gap or air break.

questions.q: In electrical wiring, what does the 'Ampacity' of a conductor represent?
o: The maximum current it can carry continuously
The maximum voltage it can carry
The resistance per foot of wire
questions.n: Ampacity is the current-carrying capacity of a wire expressed in Amperes without exceeding its temperature rating.

questions.q: Which type of HVAC system uses both a central chiller and local fan-coil units for cooling?
questions.n: All-water systems circulate chilled water to local terminals (fan coils) where the heat exchange occurs.

questions.q: What is the term for a pipe that carries clean water that has not been used, such as from a leaking valve or a water heater relief valve?
questions.n: Clear water waste refers to cooling water or condensate that does not contain impurities.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a 'Trap Seal' in a plumbing fixture?
o: To increase the velocity of the waste flow
To prevent sewer gases from entering the building
To catch lost jewelry and items
questions.n: The water held in the 'P-trap' creates a liquid seal that blocks foul odors and gases from the drainage system.

questions.q: Which unit is used to measure the rate of electric current flow?
questions.n: The ampere (or amp) is the unit that quantifies how many electrons pass a point in a second.

questions.q: In an elevator system, what is the 'Pit'?
o: The portion of the hoistway extending below the lowest floor
The heavy cables that lift the car
The room housing the hoisting machinery
questions.n: The pit provides space for the car and counterweight buffers and other equipment at the bottom of the shaft.

questions.q: What is the significance of the 'Flood Level Rim' in a plumbing fixture?
o: It is the depth of the water in the trap
It is the lowest point of the trap
It is the point where the drain connects to the stack
It is the top edge of a fixture from which water overflows
questions.n: Plumbing codes use this point to determine critical safety heights for vents and air gaps.

questions.q: What is an 'Electrical Load'?
o: Any component that consumes electrical energy
The weight of the electrical cables
A protective device for the circuit
The amount of voltage provided by the utility
questions.n: Lights, appliances, and motors are all considered loads because they convert electricity into other forms of energy.

questions.q: Which part of a building's water system maintains a constant pressure and stores a reserve for peak demand?
questions.n: Pneumatic (or pressure) tanks use compressed air to keep water under pressure and provide a buffer for the pump.

questions.q: What is the definition of a 'Branch Interval' in a drainage system?
o: The time between plumbing maintenance checks
The length of a single pipe section
A vertical distance of at least 8 feet
The distance between two fixtures on a branch
questions.n: A branch interval is a section of a soil or waste stack, usually one story high (at least 8 feet), where horizontal branches connect.

questions.q: What occurs during 'Backsiphonage'?
o: Water flows too fast through the meter
A vacuum or partial vacuum in the supply line pulls water back
The vent stack becomes clogged with debris
High pressure pushes waste into the supply
questions.n: Backsiphonage happens when negative pressure in the water main 'sucks' water from fixtures back into the system.

questions.q: In a 'Constant Air Volume' (CAV) system, how is the temperature of a room primarily controlled?
o: By changing the speed of the fan
By varying the temperature of the air supplied
By turning the entire system off and on
questions.n: CAV systems keep the flow rate steady and adjust the air temperature to meet the thermostat setting.

questions.q: What is the role of a 'Fixture Supply' pipe?
o: To measure the water used by that fixture
To connect the fixture to the drain
To connect the water-distributing pipe to the fixture
questions.n: The fixture supply is the final run of pipe that brings water directly to a faucet or valve.

questions.q: What does a 'Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter' (GFCI) protect against?
o: Low voltage from the utility company
Small current leaks that could cause electric shock
questions.n: GFCIs detect an imbalance between the 'hot' and 'neutral' wires and trip instantly to prevent electrocution.

questions.q: Which term describes the resistance of an AC circuit that includes effects from coils (inductance) and capacitors?
questions.n: Reactance is the specific opposition to AC caused by the 'reactions' of inductors and capacitors.

questions.q: What is a 'Sump' in a building's plumbing system?
o: A filter for purifying drinking water
The highest point of a drainage stack
A tank or pit that receives clear water or liquid waste
questions.n: Sumps are located below the level of the main sewer and require a pump (sump pump) to lift the waste.

questions.q: In a drainage system, what is a 'Stack'?
o: The horizontal main in the basement
A type of storage tank for hot water
Any vertical line of soil, waste, or vent piping
A group of fixtures in a row
questions.n: A stack is the general term for the main vertical pipes in a building's plumbing system.

questions.q: What does 'HVAC' stand for?
questions.n: This is the standard industry acronym for the systems that control the climate in a building.

questions.q: What is the 'Water Main'?
o: The largest pipe inside the house
A public water supply pipe controlled by a public authority
The pipe that carries waste to the septic tank
The valve that turns off the water to the sink
questions.n: The water main is the primary street pipe that serves an entire community or city block.

questions.q: Which specific device is used to monitor the current in the 'hot' and 'neutral' wires and trips the circuit if a difference as small as 5 milliamperes is detected?
questions.n: A GFCI is specifically designed to prevent electrocution by sensing the minute current imbalance caused by a ground fault.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between an 'All-Air' HVAC system and an 'All-Water' system regarding heat transfer to the conditioned space?
o: All-Air systems require more piping than All-Water systems.
All-Air systems use ducts to deliver conditioned air, while All-Water systems use pipes to deliver chilled or hot water to local terminal units.
All-Water systems provide better ventilation than All-Air systems.
All-Air systems are only for cooling, while All-Water systems are only for heating.
questions.n: The medium used to transport cooling/heating defines the system category and determines the space requirements for ducts versus pipes.

questions.q: In a drainage system, what is the 'Trap Arm'?
o: A device used to clear clogs in the trap
The portion of a fixture drain between a trap and its vent
The vertical pipe connecting a fixture to the trap
The extension of a soil stack above the highest fixture
questions.n: The trap arm is the horizontal segment where the waste flows after the trap before it reaches the air source of the vent.

questions.q: Why is 'Reactance' considered a significant factor in AC circuits involving motors?
o: It reduces the voltage drop across the long wire runs.
It represents the energy lost as heat in the motor windings.
It is the opposition to current flow caused by the magnetic fields (inductance) in the motor.
It increases the efficiency of DC motors.
questions.n: Motors use coils to create magnetic fields, which creates inductive reactance that opposes changes in current.

questions.q: What is the specific purpose of a 'Vent Cap' or 'Vent Hood' at the top of a vent stack?
o: To increase the air pressure inside the stack
To prevent water hammer in the drainage pipes
To filter sewer gases before they reach the outside air
To prevent birds, debris, or objects from entering and clogging the stack
questions.n: The cap protects the open end of the vent while still allowing air to move freely in and out.

questions.q: Which HVAC system is most suitable for a building where individual rooms require highly specific and independent temperature control simultaneously?
questions.n: VAV systems allow each zone's thermostat to adjust the air volume independently, providing localized control.

questions.q: What is the functional difference between a 'Sanitary Sewer' and a 'Storm Sewer'?
o: Storm sewers are always located inside the building.
Sanitary sewers use high pressure to move waste.
Sanitary sewers are for drinking water, and storm sewers are for waste.
Sanitary sewers carry liquid waste and fecal matter, while storm sewers carry surface run-off and rainwater.
questions.n: Segregating these allows for proper treatment of hazardous waste without overwhelming treatment plants with rain runoff.

questions.q: What component in a skyscraper elevator system is responsible for ensuring the car and counterweight remain centered and do not sway during travel?
questions.n: Guide rails are T-shaped steel tracks installed on the hoistway walls to direct the path of the car and counterweight.

questions.q: A 'Deep Well' pump is generally required when the water source is at what depth?
o: Only when the well is in a mountainous region
When the water is under high natural pressure
questions.n: Once the water table is deeper than the atmospheric limit of suction (approx. 25-30 ft), specialized deep well equipment is needed.

questions.q: What is the term for the pipe that connects the building drain to the public sewer or other place of disposal?
questions.n: The building (or house) sewer starts outside the building wall and extends to the public sewer main.

questions.q: Which electrical term refers to the rate at which work is done or energy is transformed in a circuit?
questions.n: Electrical power, measured in Watts, is the rate at which an appliance converts electricity into heat, light, or motion.

questions.q: What is the role of a 'Check Valve' in a building's water supply system?
o: To allow water to flow in only one direction
To increase the water pressure in the pipes
To shut off the water for maintenance
To regulate the flow of water to a specific fixture
questions.n: Check valves automatically close to prevent backflow if the pressure on the outlet side becomes higher than the inlet.

questions.q: In a 'Two-Pipe' HVAC system, what is the second pipe used for?
o: To supply hot water while the first supplies cold water
To serve as a return line for the water back to the central plant
To provide compressed air for the controls
To carry away condensate from the fan coil units
questions.n: A two-pipe system has one supply pipe and one return pipe for either chilled or heated water.

questions.q: What type of elevator drive is most common for low-rise buildings (2-5 stories) due to its lower cost and high lifting capacity?
questions.n: Hydraulic systems use a piston to push the car from below, which is efficient and cost-effective for shorter distances.

questions.q: What does a 'Wet Standpipe' system contain that a 'Dry Standpipe' does not?
o: A connection for the Fire Department
Water under pressure at all times
questions.n: Wet standpipes are permanently connected to a water supply, making them ready for immediate use by building occupants.

questions.q: What is the primary cause of 'Trap Siphonage' in a plumbing system?
o: Excessive water pressure in the fixture
A leak in the fixture tailpiece
A lack of proper venting leading to air pressure imbalances
The use of hot water instead of cold water
questions.n: Without a vent, flowing waste creates a vacuum that 'sucks' the water seal out of the trap, leaving it open to gases.

questions.q: In electrical wiring, which material is most commonly used as a conductor due to its high conductivity and relative affordability?
questions.n: Copper is the gold standard for building wiring because it is an excellent conductor and is very durable.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an 'Elevator Buffer'?
o: To signal the motor to slow down at a floor
To stop a descending car or counterweight at the bottom of the hoistway
To balance the weight of the passengers
To clean the guide rails as the car moves
questions.n: Buffers act as shock absorbers in the pit to safely cushion the car if it travels past the lowest floor.

questions.q: In an AC circuit, what unit measures 'Apparent Power', which is the total power delivered before accounting for the power factor?
questions.n: VA is the product of voltage and current without considering the phase shift caused by reactance.

questions.q: What is the term for an opening for the discharge of water that supplies a device not part of the plumbing system, such as a heating boiler?
questions.n: This term refers specifically to discharge points for equipment requiring water but not categorized as standard plumbing fixtures.

questions.q: Inside a cistern, what is the highest water level to which the ball valve should be adjusted to shut off?
questions.n: The waterline is the critical point in a tank or cistern where the inflow is cut off to prevent overflow.

questions.q: What is the term for a tapered device used to prevent the flow of water through the drain of a washbasin?
questions.n: A waste plug is the specific technical term for the removable stopper that allows a basin to hold water.

questions.q: An overflow pipe whose outlet is conpiscous, so that discharge from it can be observed readily, is called a:
questions.n: This pipe is positioned to alert maintenance personnel that a tank's primary shut-off mechanism has failed.

questions.q: What is the term for an outhouse or structure used specifically for the deposition of excrement?
questions.n: A privy is the classic term for an outdoor toilet facility not connected to a modern sewer system.

questions.q: Which device is an electric-motor-driven unit used for grinding food waste to be disposed of through plumbing drains?
questions.n: This is the technical name for what is commonly known as a 'garbage disposal' in residential kitchens.

questions.q: What is a loosely lined excavation in the ground which receives the discharge of a septic tank and permits effluent to seep through its sides?
questions.n: A cesspool acts as both a receiving tank and a seepage pit, though it is often considered less efficient than a modern leach field.

questions.q: What is the common term for a water closet that provides two different volume options for flushing?
questions.n: Dual-flush systems are designed to conserve water by offering a reduced flush for liquid waste.

questions.q: Which of the following factors affects the electrical resistance of a conductor?
questions.n: Resistance is dependent on the wire's length, cross-sectional area, material, and operating temperature.

questions.q: In the context of electrical circuits, what is the term for the difference in electromotive force (EMF) between any two points?
questions.n: This term describes the loss of electrical potential as current travels through a resistive element.

questions.q: What is the unit of measure for electrical potential difference?
questions.n: The volt is the standard unit used to quantify electromotive force or potential difference.

questions.q: Which device automatically provides a constant voltage supply even if the input line voltage fluctuates?
questions.n: Regulators maintain a stable output level to protect sensitive electronic equipment from surges or sags.

questions.q: What is the preferred mounting height for an electric meter base from the ground line according to many standards?
questions.n: This range ensures that the meter is easily accessible for reading and maintenance by utility personnel.

questions.q: In a service entrance pole, which device must be provided if the distance to the customer's unit is more than 50 feet (15m)?
questions.n: Additional disconnects or equipment are required at the entrance to manage long runs and ensure safety.

questions.q: What is a unit or assembly of sections and fittings forming a rigid structural system used to support cables?
questions.n: Cable trays provide an open, structured pathway for large numbers of power or data cables.

questions.q: What does the electrical acronym 'RSC' stand for?
questions.n: RSC is a heavy-duty pipe used to protect electrical wiring in harsh or exposed environments.

questions.q: In electrical systems, what is the term for a protective cover, tube, or piping system specifically for electric cables?
questions.n: Conduits are the standard protective pipes (metal or plastic) through which electrical wires are pulled.

questions.q: Which type of water is also known as 'Capillary Water'?
questions.n: Capillary water is held in small soil pores by surface tension, resisting the downward pull of gravity.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a 'Riser' and a 'Stack' in a plumbing system?
o: Stacks are only for fecal matter; Risers are for greywater.
Risers carry water supply; Stacks carry drainage or vents.
Risers are horizontal; Stacks are vertical.
questions.n: A riser is a vertical supply pipe, while a stack is a general term for vertical drainage (soil/waste) or vent pipes.

questions.q: A device used to prevent the reverse flow of water in a piping system is generally called a:
questions.n: Check valves are mechanical devices that permit flow in only one direction, automatically closing if flow reverses.

questions.q: In a septic system, what is the role of the 'Effluent'?
o: It is the solid waste that settles at the bottom of the tank.
It is the bacteria used to break down waste.
It is the scum layer that floats on top of the liquid.
It is the liquid waste that leaves the septic tank for further treatment.
questions.n: The effluent is the clarified liquid that flows out of the tank after solids have settled as sludge.

questions.q: What is the name for the vertical distance between the trap weir and the top of the dip of the trap?
questions.n: This depth of water is critical for preventing sewer gases from escaping into the room.

questions.q: In electrical terms, what is 'Inductance'?
o: The storage of electrical charge in an electric field.
The ability of a material to conduct heat.
The total resistance in a DC circuit.
Resistance to changes in electric current due to magnetic fields.
questions.n: Inductance occurs in AC circuits when magnetic fields around a conductor oppose the change in current.

questions.q: What is the function of a 'Service Head' (or weatherhead) in an electrical service entrance?
o: To prevent rain from entering the service conduit.
To step down the voltage from the utility lines.
To ground the building's electrical system.
To measure the amount of electricity used.
questions.n: The hooded shape of the weatherhead ensures that water does not travel down into the electrical meter or panel.

questions.q: In a building with a 'Direct-Upfeed' water system, what is the primary limitation?
o: It requires a large roof tank.
The height of the building is limited by the utility's street pressure.
questions.n: Street pressure can usually only push water up a few stories (approx. 3-4) without additional pumps.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a 'Circuit Breaker' compared to a 'Fuse'?
o: Fuses are more modern and safer.
A fuse is more expensive but lasts longer.
Circuit breakers only work for high voltage.
A circuit breaker can be reset after tripping; a fuse must be replaced.
questions.n: Breakers use mechanical switches to disconnect, while fuses use a metal ribbon that melts when overloaded.

questions.q: Which HVAC system type is known as a 'Central' system where all the air is treated in one location and then distributed?
questions.n: In All-Air systems, the heating or cooling is done at a central Air Handling Unit (AHU) and blown through ducts.

questions.q: In an elevator, what is the 'Car Frame'?
o: The motor that pulls the cables.
The structural steel frame that supports the elevator cab.
The decorative interior of the elevator.
The track that the elevator runs on.
questions.n: The frame carries the cab and connects it to the hoisting ropes and guide rails.

questions.q: What is the 'Working Pressure' of a plumbing system?
o: The pressure when all faucets are turned off.
The pressure during a fire emergency.
The maximum pressure a pipe is designed to operate at continuously.
The pressure required to lift water to the roof.
questions.n: Staying within the working pressure prevents pipe bursts and excessive wear on fixtures.

questions.q: In electrical wiring, what color is typically used for the 'Neutral' wire in a standard North American 120V circuit?
questions.n: White (or light grey) is the standard code color for neutral wires to ensure proper identification.

questions.q: What is a 'Unit Vent' in plumbing?
o: A vent that serves two fixtures located on the same floor.
A vent that only serves the kitchen sink.
The main vent that goes through the roof.
A mechanical fan that pulls air out of a bathroom.
questions.n: Also known as a common vent, it simplifies piping by letting two nearby fixtures share one vent stack connection.

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of a 'Traction' elevator over a 'Hydraulic' elevator?
o: It is much cheaper to install.
It does not require a machine room.
It can travel much faster and reach higher floors.
questions.n: Traction elevators use cables and counterweights, making them ideal for high-rise buildings.

questions.q: What is 'Latent Heat' in the context of HVAC?
o: Heat that can be measured with a standard thermometer.
The heat generated by the air conditioning unit itself.
Heat that causes a change in state (like humidity) without a change in temperature.
The heat lost through windows and doors.
questions.n: In HVAC, latent heat refers primarily to the energy involved in removing moisture from the air.

questions.q: In a plumbing drainage system, what is a 'Fixture Branch'?
o: The pipe that goes through the roof.
The pipe that brings water into the building.
The part of the toilet that holds water.
A horizontal pipe connecting several fixtures to a main stack.
questions.n: Branches extend from the vertical stacks to collect waste from groups of individual fixtures.

questions.q: What is an 'Electric Busway' (or Bus Duct)?
o: A large vehicle used for transporting electricians.
A prefabricated metal trough containing copper or aluminum busbars.
A type of flexible conduit used in residential homes.
The main grounding rod for a building.
questions.n: Busways are used for high-current distribution in commercial buildings as an alternative to multiple conduits.

questions.q: In an elevator, what is the 'Governor'?
o: The motor that opens and closes the doors.
The person who operates the elevator in high-end buildings.
The control panel that allows the user to pick a floor.
A speed-monitoring device that triggers the safety brakes.
questions.n: If the elevator car exceeds a safe speed, the governor mechanically trips the safeties to stop the car.

questions.q: What does a 'P-Trap' prevent from entering a building?
questions.n: The water seal in the 'U' or 'P' shape blocks toxic and foul-smelling gases from coming back up the pipes.

questions.q: What is 'Three-Phase Power' typically used for?
o: Heavy industrial machinery and large commercial HVAC motors.
questions.n: Three-phase power is more efficient for high loads and provides more consistent torque for motors.

questions.q: What is the function of an 'Air Handling Unit' (AHU)?
o: To provide emergency ventilation for fires.
To compress the refrigerant in a cooling cycle.
To heat water for the building's radiators.
To condition and circulate air as part of an HVAC system.
questions.n: The AHU contains fans, filters, and heating/cooling coils to treat air before sending it to the building.

questions.q: In a high-rise building, what is a 'Zoned' water system?
o: Providing different water for each tenant.
A system that only works in specific 'zones' of the city.
Separating drinking water from toilet water.
Dividing the building into vertical sections to manage water pressure.
questions.n: If a single system were used, the pressure at the bottom floors would be high enough to burst pipes.

questions.q: What is a 'Step-Down Transformer'?
o: A transformer that increases voltage for long-distance travel.
A safety switch that trips during a power surge.
A transformer that decreases voltage while increasing current.
A device that converts AC to DC.
questions.n: These are used to convert high-voltage utility power into safer levels for use inside a building.

questions.q: In elevator design, what is 'Interval'?
o: The time it takes to travel from the bottom to the top floor.
The distance between the guide rails.
The average time between the departure of cars from the lobby.
questions.n: Interval is a key metric in determining how long passengers have to wait for an elevator.

questions.q: What is the main function of a 'Thermostat'?
o: To measure the humidity in a room.
To blow air into the room.
To heat the water in a boiler.
To sense temperature and control the operation of HVAC equipment.
questions.n: The thermostat acts as the 'brain', turning heating or cooling on/off to reach a set point.

questions.q: In a 'Storm Drainage' system, what is a 'Leader'?
o: The main contractor in charge of the plumbing team.
A filter that removes leaves from the gutters.
The vertical pipe that carries rainwater from the roof to the ground or sewer.
The first pipe installed in a system.
questions.n: Leaders (or downspouts) are essential for moving water off the roof and away from the building foundation.

questions.q: What is 'Demand Factor' in electrical design?
o: The ratio of the maximum demand to the total connected load.
The speed at which a motor reaches full power.
The number of people demanding better lighting.
The amount of electricity a tenant is forced to pay for.
questions.n: Because not all lights and appliances are on at once, the demand factor helps size electrical equipment appropriately.

questions.q: What is a 'Wet Column' in an office building?
o: A central area where plumbing pipes are grouped to allow for easy tenant hookups.
A structural column that is leaking.
An elevator shaft that has flooded.
questions.n: Wet columns allow office tenants to install sinks or coffee stations away from the main building core.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of 'Acoustic Lining' in HVAC ducts?
o: To prevent the ducts from rusting.
To reduce the noise of air flow and mechanical equipment.
To increase the speed of the air.
To make the air smell better.
questions.n: Fiberglass or foam lining inside ducts absorbs sound so it doesn't travel into the rooms.

questions.q: In elevator systems, what are 'Safety Shoes'?
o: A type of rug placed inside the elevator car.
Mechanical sensors on the door edge that stop them from closing on a person.
Special boots worn by elevator repair workers.
The blocks that grip the guide rails during an emergency stop.
questions.n: Modern elevators often use light curtains, but physical 'safety shoes' were the traditional mechanical version.

questions.q: What is 'Greywater'?
o: Wastewater from sinks, showers, and laundry that does not contain fecal matter.
Water that has turned grey because of lead pipes.
Rainwater collected from a dirty roof.
questions.n: Greywater can often be recycled for irrigation or toilet flushing to save fresh water.
